newsitem.title: MEXICO: Salinas y Rocha close to debt accord.
newsitem.headline: Salinas y Rocha close to debt accord.

text.p: Troubled Mexican retailer Salinas y Rocha SA said on Friday it was close to reaching a debt-restructuring accord with its bank creditors.
The company said in a statement that it would give "an important part" of its properties to bank creditors as part of an eventual debt agreement.
It denied, however, recent market rumors that it planned to sell some of its retail units to a third party.
"We have the responsibility to clear up certain reports that there are negotiations to sell the company or some of its parts to a third party," Salinas y Rocha said.
"It is true the company plans to shortly conclude its debt restructuring negotiations with creditor banks, which would include payment in kind of an important part of our properties," it said.

The company, which specializes in home furnishings, was badly hit by the 1994 peso crash. Last December it said it had restructured some $450 million in debt, with creditors left holding 80 pecent of the company.
Salinas y Rocha said its recent results showed improvements across the board. It narrowed its losses to 979 million pesos in 1996 from 1.24 billion in 1995.
The company said it planned a news conference later this month to explain its first quarter results and give an update on its financial status. It did not specify a date.
